title: B-CELL IMMUNODEFICIENCY, DISTAL LIMB ANOMALIES, AND UROGENITAL MALFORMATIONS

relationships.phenotype: B-CELL IMMUNODEFICIENCY, DISTAL LIMB ANOMALIES, AND UROGENITAL MALFORMATIONS

intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that B-cell immunodeficiency, distal limb anomalies, and urogenital malformations (BILU), also known as Hoffman syndrome, is caused by heterozygous mutation in the TOP2B gene (126431) on chromosome 3p24.

checks.claim: B-cell immunodeficiency, distal limb anomalies, and urogenital malformations (BILU) is also known as Hoffman syndrome.
checks.evidence_quote: Our results indicate that BILU and Hoffman syndromes are manifestations of the same disease, TOP2B deficiency.
checks.explanation: Paper equates BILU and Hoffman syndromes as the same disease.

checks.claim: BILU (Hoffman syndrome) is caused by heterozygous mutation in the TOP2B gene.
checks.evidence_quote: Here, we show that mutations in TOP2B underlie the syndromic B-cell immunodeficiency
checks.explanation: Heterozygous TOP2B variants were found in all three families.

checks.claim: The TOP2B gene is located on chromosome 3p24.
checks.evidence_quote: One gene, TOP2B, which encodes topoisomerase IIβ, was affected by a heterozygous variant in each family
checks.explanation: The chromosomal location is standard nomenclature and is not stated in the paper.

paragraphs.text: Hoffman syndrome is an autosomal dominant disorder made up of humoral immunodeficiency with low or absent B cells and hypogammaglobulinemia, which leads to recurrent infections. It also involves anomalies of the distal limbs, such as syndactyly and other digit malformations, and malformations of the urogenital tract. Facial dysmorphism has also been described.

checks.claim: Hoffman syndrome is an autosomal dominant disorder.
checks.evidence_quote: Here, we report a second family with similar features, which also shows autosomal dominant inheritance.
checks.explanation: The abstract says both families show autosomal dominant inheritance.

checks.claim: Hoffman syndrome includes humoral immunodeficiency with low or absent B cells.
checks.evidence_quote: We report on a 7-year-old girl with almost complete loss of B cells
checks.explanation: The abstract reports an almost complete loss of B cells in the proband and an attenuated B-cell deficiency in her mother.

checks.claim: Hoffman syndrome includes hypogammaglobulinemia.
checks.evidence_quote: Laboratory evaluation revealed hypogammaglobulinaemia, absent B cells, and a 46,XX karyotype.
checks.explanation: The abstract reports hypogammaglobulinemia.

checks.claim: The immunodeficiency in Hoffman syndrome leads to recurrent infections.
checks.evidence_quote: Her clinical course has been complicated by recurrent sinopulmonary infections and pneumococcal bacteraemia.
checks.explanation: The abstract reports recurrent infections.

checks.claim: Hoffman syndrome includes distal limb anomalies such as syndactyly and other digit malformations.
checks.evidence_quote: thenar hypoplasia, partial 4-5 syndactyly of toes, recessed great toes
checks.explanation: The abstract reports syndactyly and other digit anomalies. It also gives triphalangeal thumbs among the radiographic findings.

checks.claim: Hoffman syndrome includes malformations of the urogenital tract.
checks.evidence_quote: urogenital malformations
checks.explanation: The title states that urogenital malformations are part of the syndrome.

checks.claim: Facial dysmorphism has been described in Hoffman syndrome.
checks.evidence_quote: Physical findings include microcephaly, micrognathia, sickle shaped eyebrows, hypoplastic alae nasi
checks.explanation: The title and abstract describe facial dysmorphology.

paragraphs.text: Hoffman et al. described a family in which several members across more than one generation had B-cell immunodeficiency with hypogammaglobulinemia and recurrent infections, together with distal limb anomalies and urogenital malformations. This combination became known as Hoffman syndrome.

checks.claim: Hoffman et al. described a family in which several members across more than one generation were affected.
checks.evidence_quote: We report a 6 year old girl with an isolated humoral immune deficiency and a unique combination of dysmorphic features.
checks.explanation: The paper reports one girl, not a family with several affected members across generations. Her twin is mentioned only as a developmental comparison.

checks.claim: Affected members of the family described by Hoffman et al. had B-cell immunodeficiency with hypogammaglobulinemia and recurrent infections.
checks.evidence_quote: Laboratory evaluation revealed hypogammaglobulinaemia, absent B cells, and a 46,XX karyotype.
checks.explanation: These findings are reported, but in a single patient, not in several affected family members.

checks.claim: Affected members of the family described by Hoffman et al. had distal limb anomalies.
checks.evidence_quote: Radiographic findings include triphalangeal thumbs and hypoplastic first metatarsals.
checks.explanation: The patient had distal limb anomalies, but she is the only case, not one of several affected family members.

checks.claim: Affected members of the family described by Hoffman et al. had urogenital malformations.
checks.evidence_quote: anterior anus, and hypoplastic labia minora
checks.explanation: One patient had hypoplastic labia minora and an anterior anus. This is not a family, and urogenital malformations are not described more broadly.

checks.claim: The combination of B-cell immunodeficiency, distal limb anomalies, and urogenital malformations became known as Hoffman syndrome.
checks.evidence_quote: One such report was a sporadic case of humoral immunodeficiency, facial dysmorphism, and limb anomalies in a young girl, later referred to as Hoffman syndrome.
checks.explanation: According to the abstract, the name Hoffman syndrome came from a sporadic case with humoral immunodeficiency, facial dysmorphism and limb anomalies. That original case is not described as including urogenital malformations, and it was a single sporadic patient rather than a multigenerational family.

paragraphs.text: The pattern of transmission in the family reported by Hoffman et al. fit autosomal dominant inheritance. The later finding of heterozygous TOP2B mutations confirmed this.

checks.claim: The pattern of transmission in the family reported by Hoffman et al. fit autosomal dominant inheritance.
checks.evidence_quote: She may represent a unique syndrome of unknown etiology.
checks.explanation: The paper reports one sporadic case with unknown etiology. It describes no family transmission pattern and no autosomal dominant inheritance.

checks.claim: The finding of heterozygous TOP2B mutations confirmed autosomal dominant inheritance of Hoffman syndrome.
checks.evidence_quote: Sequencing of patients with B cell-restricted immunodeficiency reveals autosomal dominant mutations in TOP2B.
checks.explanation: Heterozygous mutations consistent with dominant inheritance.

paragraphs.text: Broderick et al. (2019) studied affected members of the original Hoffman syndrome family and other patients with B-cell immunodeficiency and limb anomalies. They found heterozygous missense mutations in the TOP2B gene that segregated with the disorder. The mutations affected the catalytic domain of topoisomerase II-beta. Functional studies indicated that the mutant protein impaired enzyme function, consistent with a dominant-negative effect, and impaired B-cell development.

checks.claim: Broderick et al. (2019) studied affected members of the original Hoffman syndrome family and other patients with B-cell immunodeficiency and limb anomalies.
checks.evidence_quote: We previously reported two unrelated families with autosomal dominant inherited syndromic B-cell immunodeficiency of unknown etiology
checks.explanation: The paper studied two previously reported families plus a third patient first described as atypical Ablepharon-Macrostomia syndrome. It does not single out one 'original family' or describe the others as patients with limb anomalies.

checks.claim: Broderick et al. (2019) found heterozygous missense mutations in the TOP2B gene in patients with Hoffman syndrome.
checks.evidence_quote: a de novo in-frame deletion c.1761_1763delAGA, p.EE587E, and a missense mutation c.1448C > T, p.S483L
checks.explanation: Two variants (S483L, G633S) are missense, but one (EE587E) is an in-frame deletion, so 'missense mutations' is not accurate for all of them.

checks.claim: The heterozygous TOP2B missense mutations found by Broderick et al. (2019) segregated with the disorder.
checks.evidence_quote: We filtered variants within each family assuming that the variants would not be in dbSNP, would have a dominant inheritance pattern
checks.explanation: Pedigrees and filtering in affected vs unaffected relatives are described, but one variant is de novo and segregation is not explicitly stated.

checks.claim: The TOP2B mutations found by Broderick et al. (2019) affected the catalytic domain of topoisomerase II-beta.
checks.evidence_quote: we identified three heterozygous mutations affecting the TOPRIM, or DNA gating, domain of the type II topoisomerase TOP2B
checks.explanation: The paper specifies the TOPRIM/DNA gating domain and does not call it the catalytic domain.

checks.claim: Functional studies by Broderick et al. (2019) indicated that the mutant TOP2B protein impaired enzyme function, consistent with a dominant-negative effect.
checks.evidence_quote: demonstrate that patient mutations in TOP2B have a dominant negative effect on enzyme function
checks.explanation: Yeast and mouse studies show a dominant negative effect.

checks.claim: Functional studies by Broderick et al. (2019) indicated that the mutant TOP2B protein impaired B-cell development.
checks.evidence_quote: resulting in defective proliferation, survival of B-2 cells, causing a block in B cell development, and impair humoral function in response to immunization
checks.explanation: Mouse knockin and knockout models showed impaired B-cell development.

paragraphs.text: Papapietro et al. (2020) independently reported a heterozygous TOP2B mutation in patients with B-cell deficiency and syndromic features. A knockin mouse model showed that the mutation impaired early B-cell development.

checks.claim: Papapietro et al. (2020) independently reported a heterozygous TOP2B mutation in patients with B-cell deficiency and syndromic features.
checks.evidence_quote: This heterozygous G>C mutation at the cDNA nucleotide 1,453 of the TOP2B gene (ENST00000435706) resulted in the alanine to proline substitution at position 485 (A485P)
checks.explanation: Heterozygous TOP2B A485P in BILU patients with B-cell deficiency and limb/urogenital anomalies.

checks.claim: In a knockin mouse model by Papapietro et al. (2020), the Top2b mutation impaired early B-cell development.
checks.explanation: No mouse model is described. The early B-cell block was shown by bone marrow flow cytometry of a human patient (II:4), and the functional work used HEK-293 cells and recombinant protein.

paragraphs.text: Papapietro et al. (2020) found that mice carrying a Top2b mutation corresponding to the human mutation had defective early B-cell development. This reproduced the B-cell deficiency seen in patients.

checks.claim: Papapietro et al. (2020) found that mice carrying a Top2b mutation corresponding to the human TOP2B mutation had defective early B-cell development.
checks.explanation: The paper describes no mice carrying a Top2b mutation; the evidence on B-cell development comes from patient bone marrow.

checks.claim: The defective B-cell development in the Top2b mutant mice of Papapietro et al. (2020) reproduced the B-cell deficiency seen in patients.
checks.explanation: No animal model is reported in the paper.
